e: ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory store with native geospatial commands and very fast reads and writes, so placing it in front of the database absorbs the rapid location updates and lookups as the user base grows. DAX only works with DynamoDB, and Multi-AZ or OpenSearch don't address write throughput.

DynamoDB deletion protection prevents a table from being deleted accidentally, with a single setting and no operational overhead. Backups, PITR, or automated restore scripts recover after the loss rather than preventing it.

A cached volume gateway stores the data in S3 and keeps a local cache of frequently accessed data, which relieves on-premises capacity, minimizes bandwidth use, and gives immediate access to hot data at no retrieval fees. Glacier expedited retrieval costs extra, and stored volumes keep all data on premises.

Predictive scaling analyzes daily and weekly historical load patterns to forecast and scale ahead, and dynamic scaling with target tracking reacts to live changes in utilization, covering both forecast and real-time needs. Step, scheduled, or simple scaling alone don't combine both.

The load comes from repeated identical read statements, so an ElastiCache for Redis cache between the application and the database serves them from memory, taking load off the cluster at lower cost than more replicas. More replicas or Auto Scaling keep paying for replicated reads, and Aurora writers don't help reads.

DynamoDB reads are eventually consistent by default, so some reads return stale data. Requesting strongly consistent reads returns the latest data, and since latency is acceptable, that tradeoff fits. DynamoDB has no read replicas, and a GSI supports only eventually consistent reads.

AWS WAF protects the application from SQL injection and other web attacks with managed rules and little setup, and RDS parameter groups configure database security settings. Security groups and network ACLs don't inspect web requests, and Network Firewall or per-function accounts add effort.

The GuardDuty RDS Protection feature analyzes login activity on Aurora databases and detects anomalous and failed login attempts, and it can be enabled across the organization's member accounts, which is the most operationally efficient way. SCPs, general logs, or CloudTrail events don't detect abnormal logins.

A Direct Connect gateway lets one Direct Connect connection reach VPCs in multiple Regions (via virtual private gateways or transit gateways), and with the acquired company's connection attached, it connects both Regions and both data centers at scale with low overhead. Inter-Region peering doesn't cover on-premises, and EC2 VPN meshes are operationally heavy.

Kinesis Data Streams absorbs traffic spikes and preserves ordering within a shard, Lambda processes the records with no servers, and DynamoDB is a highly available database for results, all with minimal management. Redshift or EC2 databases, and unordered SNS, miss the requirements.

S3 Same-Region Replication copies logs from each account's bucket to a central bucket in us-west-2 automatically, keeping data in the Region with no code to run, at the lowest cost. Lifecycle policies can't copy objects, and scripts or Lambda functions add operational work.

Bidirectional replication among the three buckets keeps the data in sync no matter where uploads happen, and an S3 Multi-Region Access Point lets the application use a single endpoint (ARN) for both streaming and uploads, routing to the closest bucket for the lowest latency with the fewest application changes.

Because users consume 90% of the content in the Region where it's uploaded and content is short-lived, uploading to an S3 bucket in the Region closest to the user gives the lowest upload latency and keeps delivery local, with CloudFront for delivery. A single bucket with Transfer Acceleration or CloudFront uploads still routes to one far Region.

API Gateway can send requests to Amazon EventBridge, whose rules filter events by content and invoke only the Lambda functions that need each message, with the least operational overhead. Adding SQS queues, MSK, or manual fan-out to queues adds components to manage.

An S3 Inventory report identifies the existing unencrypted objects, an S3 Batch Operations job re-encrypts them with a customer-provided key, and default encryption configured for new objects covers future uploads, as the requirement for customer-provided keys (SSE-C) demands. KMS options don't use customer-provided keys, and usage reports can't list objects.

Create a Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain and import the existing zone file to quickly copy the records, then update the registrar's name servers, giving a resilient managed DNS service on AWS. Private hosted zones are for VPCs, Simple AD isn't DNS hosting, and Resolver endpoints don't host public zones.

AWS AppConfig manages application configuration, and Secrets Manager securely stores and retrieves database credentials (with rotation), both managed with low overhead. Lambda isn't a configuration store, S3 files are insecure for credentials, and RDS can't store its own credentials.

To encrypt data in transit to RDS, connect with SSL/TLS by downloading the AWS-provided root certificates and using them in all connections. Self-signed certificates aren't used by RDS, IAM authentication is not encryption in transit, and restoring a snapshot concerns encryption at rest.

A Network Load Balancer can be assigned a static Elastic IP address per Availability Zone, giving clients fixed IP addresses to allow on their firewalls. ALBs don't support Elastic IPs, and a single EC2 proxy or a Route 53 record to an Elastic IP isn't a load balancer solution.

Best practice is to create IAM users (or roles) for daily administration and secure the root user with multi-factor authentication. The root user can't be disabled, and root access keys or sharing root credentials are unsafe.

Enhanced networking gives higher bandwidth and lower latency between instances, and a cluster placement group places instances close together in one AZ for the lowest inter-node latency. Separate accounts, multiple ENIs, and EBS optimization don't lower network latency between nodes.

DataSync migrates millions of small files and preserves the directory structure and SMB metadata, and FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB file shares so applications keep accessing data the same way without changes. Lustre isn't SMB, S3 changes the access method, and volume gateway is block storage.

CloudWatch cross-account observability lets a designated monitoring account query and visualize metrics, logs, and traces from source accounts, set up by linking accounts (for example, with a CloudFormation template from the monitoring account). IAM users and SCPs don't provide this centralized view.

The website uses AWS WAF with CloudFront, so adding an IP match (IP set) rule to the web ACL blocks the malicious IP address at the edge. Network ACLs and security groups can't block CloudFront-forwarded clients properly (security groups have no deny rules), and CloudFront has no network ACL.

IAM Identity Center connects to the existing identity provider (through SAML/SCIM), provisions users and groups, and gives the employees single sign-on access to all accounts in the organization at scale. IAM users, root users, or RAM sharing don't provide federated access to accounts.
